messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] router-usw2.p99_latency > 3.0s for 5m (auto-page: oncall)
amira (oncall): paging @ryan and @david — p99 is spiking to ~4.8s, customers report streaming stalls. I’m booting the triage channel.
ryan (sre): on it. pulling up graphs now — p95 jumped to 1.2s -> 2.4s, p99 0.9s -> 4.8s in last 10m. tail latency looks like queuing on router->shard hop. logs show increased 503->retry bursts for long-stream sessions.
david (eng-runtime): I deployed the routing-weight-policy change at 08:12 UTC (canary then rollout). It adjusted per-customer affinity weight calculation to favor affinity_buckets. Could be a bug where hotkeys are being pinned to a single hot shard.
amira (oncall): priya, any inbound CS reports? priya (support): ACME corp webhook reported repeated stream stalls and connection resets since ~08:20 UTC. They see chunked responses pause > 10s then resume. Escalated to enterprise-support.
ryan (sre): quick checks: KV cache hit rate for router shard s-07 dropped from 98% -> 61% at 08:18. That aligns w/ a hotshard getting most traffic and cold cache elsewhere.
ryan (sre): running quick query:

```
# - kusto style
requests
| where service == "router-usw2"
| summarize p95=percentile(latency,95), p99=percentile(latency,99) by bin(timestamp, 1m)
| where timestamp > ago(15m)
```
Output: p99=4.8s @ 08:21, p95=2.3s @ 08:21
amira (oncall): okay hypothesis: new weight policy caused skew -> hot partition -> cache misses/queueing -> streaming stalls. Need live mitigation.
david (eng-runtime): options: 1) revert weight-policy feature flag to previous config (fast), 2) force rebalancing: temporarily add routing fuzz to spread affinity, 3) shift heavy customers to fallback pool. Revert is safest.
ryan (sre): prefer revert first. Can someone flip the flag? I’ll prepare rollback plan and watch queues.
ops-bot: deploy-rollout: weight-policy-v2 revert initiated by david at 08:25 UTC. CI checks pass (config-only). Rolling to router-usw2 first.
david (eng-runtime): reverted weight-policy-v2 on router-usw2 at 08:26 UTC. Confirming config checksum.
amira (oncall): monitoring p99 and KV hit-rate.
ryan (sre): immediate signal: p99 dropped from 4.8s -> 2.0s by 08:28. KV cache hit rates trending back up to 94% on affected shards.
priay: (support): ACME says stream stalls reduced after ~08:29 and errors gone by 08:31. They want incident update and root cause.
amira (oncall): marking customer impact: ACME corp (enterprise) — intermittent streaming stalls, degraded p99, impacted for ~11m. Notified CS and account team.
ryan (sre): follow-up mitigation: schedule full rollout rollback to all regions and add circuit-breaker guard to weight-policy that prevents >X% of traffic being pinned to single shard. Adding metric alert for affinity-skew.
david (eng-runtime): will push patch: reject affinity assignment if bucket weight > 0.6 of pool (safety). Also add explicit rebalancing when imbalance detected.
amira (oncall): oncall handoff note: leaving triage to ryan to run postmortem. I’ll annotate timeline in the incident tracker.
ryan (sre): opened incident ticket INC-2026-1745, capturing timeline + mitigation steps. Will coordinate postmortem with eng-runtime & support. Tentative RCA: routing-weight-policy v2 produced affinity skew on certain key distribution, leading to hot shard, KV cache thrash, streaming stalls and elevated p99.
ops-bot: pager closed by amira at 08:40 UTC (condition: p99 < 2.5s & KV hit-rate > 90% for 5m)
amira (oncall): nice work. Action items: (1) full rollback across regions (david), (2) add affinity-skew alert & circuit breaker (david/ryan), (3) customer update template sent (priay), (4) postmortem in 48h with corrective plan (ryan).
ryan (sre): will run through replay: add tests for hotkey distributions against synthetic load. Also check whether rollout gating lacked skew detection — follow-up on rollout tooling.
priay (support): ACME follow-up: submitted update telling them we reverted change and are investigating; they requested root-cause and ETA for prevention. I’ll route to AE and Legal if needed.
amira (oncall): closing slack thread for live mitigation. Keep thread updated if any regressions. postmortem assigned to @ryan and @david. :memo:
